tool_input.description: Probe actual runtime behavior of DurationFormatUtils for edge cases
Probe HMS rollover and null format handling

result:
34 of 36 tests pass. The 2 failures are the two bugs I intentionally wrote tests for, confirming the code's actual (buggy) behavior diverges from its documented contract.

Both remaining failures confirm real bugs in `DurationFormatUtils`:

1. **`testFormatDurationISOMatchesJavadocExample`** — `formatDurationISO`'s own javadoc says it formats "the days and lower fields... such as `P7D6TH5M4.321S`", but `ISO_EXTENDED_FORMAT_PATTERN` isn't optional-wrapped for years/months, so the method always emits the always-zero year/month fields, producing `P0Y0M7DT6H5M4.321S` instead of the documented `P7D6TH5M4.321S`.

2. **`testSameLetterTokenSeparatedByLiteralAreIndependentOccurrences`** — in `lexx()`, the `previous` token reference used to merge repeated-letter tokens (e.g. `"dd"` → one field of width 2) is never reset when a literal (or optional-block boundary) intervenes. So pattern `"d'x'd"` with 5 days produces `"5x"` instead of `"5x5"`: the second `d` occurrence is silently swallowed into the first token's count rather than rendered at its own position.
